description: Native CPU decoder versus GPU decoders (octree and Gaussian), decoding the same saved latents of the published Idol-Q8_0.gguf.
device: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090 (24,564 MiB), 32 logical CPUs, Windows 11, PyTorch 2.10.0+cu128
inputs: The saved latents of three GSO32 objects (first, 13th and 25th in protocol order), seed 42, 262,144 Gaussians; three repeats per decoder after one warm-up for the GPU decoders.

decoders.native_cpu: build/idol_decode (build_fresh), IDOL_QUANT_KERNEL=float, 4 and 8 threads, decoder cache built in 2.84 s
decoders.gpu: upstream mixed-precision decoders with fused packed kernels; load 1.88 s, 305.3 MiB of resident weights

objects.timing_note: Native CPU timings for this object are not usable: another heavy Idol workload on the same machine was running at the time (the 8-thread median is slower than the 4-thread one).

summary.speed: On the two objects measured without interference the GPU decoders took 0.3 to 1.2 s and the native decoder 57 to 62 s with 4 threads and 37 to 38 s with 8 threads, roughly 30 to 180 times slower.
summary.memory: The native decoder peaked at 818 MiB (4 threads) and 823 MiB (8 threads) of process working set. The GPU decoders peaked at 523 MiB of PyTorch-allocated device memory (305 MiB of it resident weights).
summary.agreement: Both decoders agree with the original-Idol mesh to the same degree: mean mesh distance / diagonal 0.065% (GPU) and 0.064% (CPU), 0.087% and 0.088%, and 0.076% and 0.076% on the three objects. They differ from each other by 0.037% to 0.053% of the diagonal, less than either differs from the original.

limits: The two decoders use different random number generators, so a fixed seed does not give identical point clouds; agreement is measured on meshes extracted with the protocol settings.
Timings come from a shared workstation and single sessions of three repeats; the GPU decoders ran with other GPU work active. They show the order of magnitude, not a latency distribution.
CPU peak is the process working set; GPU peak is PyTorch allocated memory, which excludes the CUDA context. They are not directly comparable figures.
Three objects at one seed, not a cohort.
